narrative:
The 2025 Pittsburgh Pirates entered the season with cautious optimism, leaning on veteran presence and a pitching staff that proved more capable than most expected. Early in the year, familiar faces and surprising contributors delivered moments of genuine excitement — Tommy Pham's clutch RBI single in April and Andrew McCutchen's timely double at the end of the month reminded Pittsburgh fans that the old guard still had something left. The offense was fragile, posting a modest .655 OPS, but when the pieces clicked together, the Pirates could beat anyone.

May became the most electric stretch of the Pirates' season. Alexander Canario announced himself with a three-run home run, and then came the wild May 23rd roller coaster — David Bednar's blown save nearly undid everything, before Oneil Cruz launched his tenth home run of the year and Canario followed with a clutch single to seal the win. That evening encapsulated the Pirates perfectly: maddening vulnerability giving way to improbable resilience. A week later, Isiah Kiner-Falefa's double capped another rally, and for a brief moment Pittsburgh looked like a team capable of climbing in the standings.

The summer months told a harsher story. The bullpen became a recurring source of heartbreak, with Dennis Santana surrendering critical home runs on three separate occasions, including a devastating two-run blast on August 1st that swung win probability by more than 80 percentage points. Mitch Keller coughed up a pivotal late-game homer in July, and the offense too often went quiet at the wrong moments. Bryan Reynolds provided flashes of brilliance — none more beautiful than his August 8th triple that plated two runs — and Joey Bart's clutch single days earlier showed the young catcher's promise, but the wins simply weren't coming fast enough.

By September, the Pirates were playing out the string on a 71-91 season. McCutchen provided one last sentimental highlight with a two-RBI single on September 13th, a reminder of what he had meant to Pittsburgh across two stints. But Tommy Pham's late-season double play and more Santana heartbreak in the final week confirmed the team's fate. Pittsburgh finished 20 games under .500, their pitching staff surprisingly respectable at a 3.76 ERA but their anemic offense — only 583 runs scored — never giving that staff enough margin for error. The 2025 Pirates were not without character or moments worth remembering, but they were a team still searching for the identity that might one day return them to October.

chapters.title: Veterans Lead the Way
chapters.description: Tommy Pham and Andrew McCutchen provide early sparks as Pittsburgh shows signs of life in April.

chapters.title: The May Surge
chapters.description: An explosive run of clutch hits and home runs — headlined by Canario and Cruz — gives Pirates fans genuine reason for hope.

chapters.title: Summer Unraveling
chapters.description: A string of bullpen collapses and costly home runs allowed derail Pittsburgh's momentum through July and into August.

chapters.title: Flickers in the Dark
chapters.description: Reynolds, Bart, and Suwinski deliver individual highlights, but the Pirates cannot sustain any winning consistency.

chapters.title: Fading Into September
chapters.description: McCutchen's farewell moment and more late-season bullpen failures confirm a disappointing 71-91 finish for Pittsburgh.
